For 43 years, Cuba has protected Hill from facing charges for killing a New Mexico police officer and hijating an airplane to Havana. Hill, now 65, decided to give CNN an interview after we spent two years trying to reach him. He wants to talk about how for the first time he is thinking about leaving his safe place and going back to the United States.

Misao Okawa, who was the oldest living person in the world, has died at the age of 117. She passed on Wednesday morning in Osaka, Japan. Tadahi Uchimura, a city official, told CNN. Okawa leaves behind three children, four grandchildren, and six great-grandchildren. Okawa was born on March 5, 1898. Her family owned a kimono shop in Osaka. Satoshi Yoshioka, who works at the nursing home where Okawa has lived since 1997, told CNN. "She was a kind person, and loved to eat so much. Her favorite food was sushi and udon noodles," Yoshioka said. "She has eaten a lot of cake for her birthday last March 5."

The Guard went to Ferguson to support police officers. Many community leaders and civil rights activists accused the police of using too much force and making the already tense situation worse during the protests, which happened off and on from August until the end of the year.

Mogadishu, Somalia (CNN) — Gunmen attacked the Somali education ministry in the capital on Tuesday. They came after a suicide car bomb. The attack killed at least 12 people and injured 16 others, officials said. The Islamist militant group Al-Shabaab claimed responsibility for the attack in central Mogadishu, group spokesman Abu Musab said. The attack started when two suicide bombers blew up their car at the entrance of the two-story building. The building houses the Ministry of Education, Culture and Higher Education, Somali National Security Ministry spokesman Mohamed Yusuf said. Five gunmen then entered the building and shot people inside, Yusuf said.

One war was enough for 87-year-old Gregory Margolin. When he was 16, he fought in the Soviet Red Army during World War II. As he fought the Nazis, his family had to run away. Margolin says, “I kept quiet about being Jewish. But it didn’t matter because people were being killed all around me.” Now, in Ukraine, he is facing war again. Margolin was a a sharp shooter and became a a leader in the army. his old uniform still has medals from his time in the army. his granddaughter Liora still thinks his war stories are amazing. she is surprised that he lived through it.

 Norway has 5 million people. Many people there have already made the switch. On FM radio, there are only five stations. On digital radio, there are four times as many stations. Half of the country now listens to digital radio, according to Culture Minister Thorhild Widvey.

Everyone is big fan of a good comeback story, especially when it involves dinosaurs. A new study suggests that the Brontosaurus is back. It was its own type of dinosaur, and should keep its own name. For more than a century, science books said the Brontosaurus was not its own type.

 O.C. Marsh first named the Brontosaurus in 1879. He got 55 crates of bones from Como Bluff in Wyoming, according to the Yale Peabody Museum of Natural History. The Brontosaurus was similar to the Apatosaurus, but smaller than it. The Apatosaurus was found a few years before. Marsh named the dinosaur, "Brontosaurus," or "thunder lizard."

Freddie Gray, 25, died in police custody 15 days ago after he was arrested on a weapons charge. He died from a severe spinal cord injury. His death caused widespread anger toward the Baltimore Police Department. Gray’s death is the latest in a series of high-profile deaths involving African-Americans and law enforcement. Many people demanded answers about what happened to Gray. His funeral drew civil rights leaders, politicians, and relatives of others who died in police custody. A white casket sat at the front of New Shiloh Baptist Church in West Baltimore as a gospel choir sang for a large crowd gathered to honor Freddie Gray.

Dan Swangard is a doctor. He has seen many patients dying in hospitals. They were connected to machines and given strong pain medicine. Swangard watched as their families stood by, feeling helpless and scared. Sometimes, death took weeks or even months.

A Saudi source told CNN that Saudi special forces helped Yemeni fighters fight against Houthi rebels and their allies in Aden. The special forces were in Yemen to help organize and guide the battle, but they did not fight themselves. They also helped drop off weapons and communication equipment by parachute. The source said that Houthi rebels left the presidential palace and other important places in the southern port city of Aden after strong Saudi air attacks. This withdrawal was a change from the previous day, when Houthi forces took control of the presidential palace.

On April 27, South Africa marks the anniversary of the first post-apartheid elections held in 1994. This year, we are facing another wave of deadly attacks against African migrants. The anger caused by this violence is being heard loudly on social media, with the hashtag "#WeAreAfrica" showing the need for a united front against this attack. These repeated attacks on migrants and their property may be seen as another sign that the "rainbow nation" dream has failed. That vision was not only about a multi-ethnic South Africa, but also about living with dignity across racial and class lines.

In 1989, Iran’s leader, Ayatollah Khomeini, admitted that he was “drinking poison” when he agreed to a ceasefire to end the eight-year war with Iraq. The war had helped make the Islamic Republic, which he had created the year before Iraq’s leader Saddam Hussein attacked Iran. Khomeini inspired both his supporters and his growing critics to fight against the enemy. He kept the war going for eight years, even though Saddam was ready to stop fighting, and in doing so he made the Islamic Republic stronger. When the war finally ended, Iran’s economy was in terrible shape, and there was no sign of his most loyal volunteers.

The idea of sustainable development is that unchecked capitalism is too powerful for its own good. The global economy is growing very fast, and it doubles in size every generation. However, the Earth is limited in size, and the population is increasing by one billion people every 15 years. This rapid growth is damaging the natural environment and the social systems that make life good. Sustainable development offers a way to solve this growing problem. The truth is that unchecked capitalism is driven by greed.

The United States has many benefits from being a space power. U.S. access to space helps our national security, defense, and the economy. Our military uses space tools like intelligence, GPS, and communication satellites to fight current and future conflicts, combat terrorism, and handle threats around the world. However, as global threats grow and the need for reliable space access increases, the U.S. has a serious problem: we rely too much on Russian technology to meet our national security needs.

A university in South Africa is celebrating the removal of a statue of Cecil Rhodes, a British colonial leader. after weeks of protests. Students at the University of Cape Town used social media to demand the statue be taken down. They said his legacy is stained with racism. Using the hashtag #RhodesMustFall, students shared their views in a campaign that started last month. Four weeks later, the hashtag is now #RhodesHas Fallen. Syria is a terrible place, things are worse, and more people are dying. The death toll has doubled in one year, according to an opposition group. The Syrian Observatory for Human Rights said 310,00 people have been killed since the civil war started. A year before that, the number was 162,402.
